payload.headline: Apple dips to 349.21; still above every value estimate as forecasts slip

summary.thesis: Apple is a highly profitable business that produces a lot of cash, but at 349.21 the price assumes much faster cash growth than the company is delivering, and analysts keep lowering their forecasts.
summary.decision: Long term: wait, and do not buy above 300.56. Swing: wait, because the price is moving sideways just under resistance.
summary.act_at: Buy at or below 300.56; add at 265.6

payload.happening: Apple closed at 349.21, down 0.92% on the day, inside a sideways range with resistance at 354.14–356.08 and support at 342.73–345.08. Analysts cut their next-quarter earnings-per-share forecast by 3.8% over 30 days, to 2.15. Separately, the FT and TechCrunch reported that the UK lost its bid to keep a secret Apple 'backdoor' order hidden. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-28.
payload.business: What changes the business: sales are still growing, but more slowly. Sales grew 11.72% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, down from 16.6% two quarters ago. Margins improved, with operating margin (profit from operations as a share of sales) at 33.01%, up from 31.97%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. The real warning sign is in the filings: inventory rose 154% while quarterly sales rose 12%. Unsold product can force price cuts, which would hit margins. Falling analyst forecasts point the same way. What changes only sentiment or governance: the reported UK backdoor dispute is about privacy and government pressure. It does not directly change demand or cash today. The new investigation risk in the annual report is also a governance issue for now. At risk: the growth rate and margins if the inventory build turns into discounting. Not at risk: the balance sheet in the near term. Liquidity is 56.7B against net debt of 23.4B, and the share count fell 1.56% in a year.

worth.text: At 349.21, Apple trades at 38.9 times trailing earnings and 32.9 times next year's expected earnings. It is priced at 10.6 times sales, against a peer median of 5.3, and that sales multiple sits at the 98th percentile of its own 5-year history. A discounted cash flow model (DCF: it values the company by estimating future cash and converting it to today's dollars, using a 10.1% discount rate) gives 141.64 in the bear case, 196.25 in the base case and 256.62 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. To justify today's price, free cash flow would need to start growing at about 27.2% a year. Sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years. Starting growth is the assumption that drives the gap between methods. At 20% starting growth the value is 265.6. At 30% it is 388.34. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 24%, the value would be 198.8. My range runs from the DCF base case to the top of Apple's own history.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free-cash-flow growth: the price needs about 27.2% a year, while sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 136.1B from 98.8B a year earlier, so the cash engine is getting stronger.
Operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%, which shows pricing power and cost control so far.
If free cash flow starts growing at 30%, the model value is 388.34, above today's price.
bear: Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, which could force discounts and lower margins.
Analysts cut next-quarter EPS forecasts by 3.8% over 30 days, and next-year forecasts by 2.3%.
Price-to-sales of 10.6 is about double the peer median of 5.3 and sits at the 98th percentile of Apple's own 5-year history, so there is little room for disappointment.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 141.64–300.56, so it is too high to buy.

The top of my range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, close to the rising 200-day average (the average closing price over the last 200 days) of 302.45. Buying starts to make sense at or below this level.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still above last year's sales growth. Adding is justified here.

longterm.why: The business is high quality and generates a lot of cash, but the price needs much faster growth than Apple is delivering, and forecasts are falling. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price is moving sideways in the 347.89–351.46 zone, with resistance starting at 354.14 and a typical daily move (ATR) of 7.75, so there is little room to gain before resistance. The macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 356.08, or on a pullback that holds the 342.73–345.08 support zone.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.7% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.7% move by 2027-02-19, which includes the 2027-01-28 report; there is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: The price falls to 300.56 or lower: this moves the stance from wait to buy.
The 2027-01-28 report shows quarterly sales growth back above 16.6% and operating margin holding at 33.01% or higher despite the inventory build: this would support the faster-growth case.
The next-year EPS consensus rises back above 10.84, its level 30 days ago: this would show the forecast cuts have stopped.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait on both horizons, confirmed by another cut to forecasts, with next-quarter EPS down 3.8% in 30 days while the price of 349.21 stays above the 300.56 top of the value range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
